page: Vultr vhp-12c-24gb-intel is a High Performance family virtual server featuring 12 shared vCPUs mapped to 6 physical Intel Xeon cores with hyper-threading enabled. Operating on the x86_64 architecture at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz, the processor includes a 16 MB L3 cache, 4 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1d cache. The system is equipped with 24.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Local storage is bundled with a 500 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data places this server consistently in the average performance tier across most compute and memory operations. The stress-ng multi-core test yields a score of 17309.27, while the single-core performance registers at 1418.58. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block cached speed of 1224.9 GB/sec, which drops to 87.74 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, alongside a write speed of 47.62 GB/sec. Cryptographic and vector processing capabilities are supported by hardware flags such as AVX-512 and AES, resulting in a PassMark CPU encryption score of 6545.88.

While the server demonstrates capable performance for lightweight tasks, it exhibits distinct limitations under heavier workloads. For instance, LLM inference speeds for a small 135M model reach 142.19 tokens/sec for text generation, but drop to a weak 7.43 tokens/sec when processing a medium 7B model. The shared CPU allocation introduces potential resource contention, making it less suitable for sustained, high-intensity compute tasks. However, with a PassMark database score of 4095.21 and Redis SET performance at 18.53 million operations per second, this configuration is suited for web serving, database operations, and moderate multi-threaded decompression tasks.
description: Vultr vhp-12c-24gb-intel is a High Performance virtual server configured with 12 shared vCPUs across 6 physical Intel Xeon cores, 24.0 GB of RAM, and a 500 GB NVMe SSD. Operating on the x86_64 architecture at 2.0 GHz, this instance delivers a balanced compute-to-memory ratio of 1:2. Benchmark results indicate average performance across standard operations, with a PassMark CPU score of 17934.88 and a multi-core stress-ng score of 17309.27. The server handles lightweight workloads efficiently, achieving 18.53 million Redis SET operations per second and 11.99 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. However, the shared CPU allocation and a weak 7.43 tokens/sec text generation speed on 7B LLM models represent clear tradeoffs for sustained or heavy compute tasks. It is best suited for database operations, web serving, and moderate multi-threaded applications.
